title: Pinsker's inequality for finite KL divergence
statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be probability measures on a measurable space $\Omega$, and suppose that the Kullback–Leibler divergence $\mathrm{KL}(\mu \,\|\, 
u)$ is finite. Then the total variation distance $\mathrm{TV}(\mu,
u) = 	frac{1}{2}\|\mu - 
u\|_{\mathrm{TV}}$ satisfies
\[
  2\,\mathrm{TV}(\mu,
u)^2 \;\le\; \mathrm{KL}(\mu \,\|\, 
u).
\]
hypotheses_covered: $\mu$ and $\nu$ are probability measures on a measurable space $\Omega$
replaced:
If $\mathrm{KL}(\mu \| \nu) \ne \infty$, then
\[
  2\,\mathrm{TV}(\mu,\nu)^2 \;\le\; \mathrm{KL}(\mu \| \nu).\mathrm{toReal},
\]
providing a real-valued form of Pinsker's inequality convenient when finiteness of
the KL divergence is already known.
